EventId.description: A lowercase hyphenated version 7 UUID identifying one event.
EventId.title: EventId

EventKind.description: The name one kind of event is written down under: lowercase `snake_case`, declared by the domain that owns the event.
EventKind.title: EventKind

EventRecord.description:
One event, as the store holds it and the server serves it.

`raw` holds the bytes exactly as received for an externally sourced event
and is absent for an internally raised one — it is what makes the history
auditable when a normalization turns out to be wrong. `print_id` is
optional, because an externally sourced event may name no print this system
knows.

id.description: This event's identifier, minted by the store.

image.description: The image it arrived with, when it arrived with one.

payload.description: What it carries, in the form its kind declares.

print_id.description: The print it belongs to, when it belongs to one.

raw.description: The bytes exactly as received, for an externally sourced event.

EventSource.description: Where an event came from, as the bare string the domain that raised it declares for itself.
EventSource.title: EventSource

ImageFallback.description: Why a check or a look was shown the whole frame.

message.description: The reason, in the sentence the image's note gives it in.

ImageId.description: A lowercase hyphenated version 7 UUID identifying one image.
ImageId.title: ImageId

ImageKind.description: Which image a check or a look was shown.

oneOf.description:
The three panels: the frame with this layer's plan drawn on it, a
close-up of the part, and the previous check's frame.
The camera's frame, scaled whole and uncropped, nothing drawn.

ImageRef.description: The handle an image travels in context under.

sha256.description: The SHA-256 of its bytes, lowercase hexadecimal.

PrintId.description: A lowercase hyphenated version 7 UUID identifying one print.
PrintId.title: PrintId

PrinterState.description:
The state a source reports a printer or a print to be in.

The `unknown` arm exists so that a state nobody anticipated is recorded
carrying the source's own word for it rather than lost.

oneOf.description: Connected and idle.
Printing, but paused.
Printing.
Cancelling a print.
In an error state.
Not reachable.
A state this vocabulary does not name, in the source's own word for it.

Timestamp.description: An instant in UTC, as an RFC 3339 string with a zero offset.
Timestamp.title: Timestamp

WholeFrameReasonCode.description:
Why a check or a look was shown the whole frame: one code per reason the
server gives one.

oneOf.description: No print is named: a look at the printer.
No camera calibration is configured.
No camera snapshot address is configured.
The print's G-code index gives no file position for the check.
The G-code names no extruded object laid at that point.
It names no layer there.
The layer's planned toolpath could not be read back.

The print's first layer is not down, or no frame of it has been judged
yet.

The last frame judged could not tell where the first layer lies: the
toolhead covered the part, or the layer was not clearly found. A later
check's frame is judged again. No evidence of a defect.
The print's G-code lays no object to align.
The camera's frames cannot be judged against the calibration.

Fewer than two landmarks are found, so whether the camera shifted is
unknown.
The camera moved since the drawing's correction was taken.

The landmarks show the camera has moved since its calibration, so the
plan cannot be drawn reliably on its frames: the camera wants
recalibrating.
The frame is not the calibration's size or stream.

The printer reports the print paused, its bed moved off the plan's
height.
The composer refused the frame for another reason.

description:
What the supervisor knew about the moment one turn began, beside its event.

Facts rather than instructions: whether the print is paused, and whether
the detector paused it itself, are exactly what decides whether an agent's
adjustment would be applied to a moving print or held until it moves again.
Every field is written out, a fact nobody knows as `null`, so that the
prompt it fills has one shape whatever was known.

arrived_while_busy.description:
Events for this print that arrived while its previous turn was running
and that turn never took, oldest first. The turn's own event is the
newest of them, and is not repeated here.

detector_paused_the_print.description:
Whether the detector paused the print itself, null when the event is
not one of its detections.

detector_warned.description:
Whether the detector only warned, null when the event is not one of its
detections.

frame_captured_at.description:
When the frame an alert brought was captured, which its source says or the
moment it answered; absent when the event says so itself or has no frame.

image.description:
What the image attached to the prompt is, and why it is that one, in
one line; absent when no image is attached or what made it says
nothing.

image_fallback.description:
Why the attached image is the whole frame; absent for the three-panel
image, when no image is attached, or when what made it gave no reason.

image_kind.description: Which image is attached to the prompt; absent when none is.

noticed.description:
What the printer watch noticed that prompted this turn — how the print
ended, what the printer did on its own after it, that the camera gave
no usable frame, that the failure detector stopped answering — in
words beginning with the event's kind; null when the turn was prompted
by anything else.

printer_state.description:
The printer's state when the turn began, in the printer contract's own
vocabulary — a state it does not name as `{"unknown": "<the printer's
word>"}` — null when the printer could not be read.

title: TurnSituation
